messages.content: I need to write to my younger brother about the welding machine. He’s missed three €250 payments now, and I want to be firm about the money without making it sound like a threat. Can you help me phrase it?

Sure—here’s a firm but respectful version:

> Hi [Name], I need to sort out the payments for the welding machine. The last three €250 payments haven’t been made, so the outstanding amount is now €750. Please let me know by [date] when you can pay this, or suggest a realistic repayment plan if you can’t pay it all at once. I want to keep this straightforward and avoid any tension between us, but I do need the agreed payments to be kept up with. Thanks.

That is close. I’m worried that “by [date]” may sound like an ultimatum, and he probably can’t pay the €750 all at once. I’d rather ask him to commit to a specific date for the next €250 and tell me what schedule he can realistically manage after that.

Hi [Name], I wanted to follow up about the welding machine payments. The last three €250 payments are still outstanding, so I’d appreciate it if you could let me know a specific date when you can make the next €250 payment. It would also help if you could tell me what repayment schedule you can realistically manage for the remaining balance. I understand you may not be able to pay the full €750 at once—I just need us to agree on a clear plan and keep to it.

Yes, this is better. I’d maybe say “the rest of the amount you owe” instead of “remaining balance,” since the €750 is only the three missed installments. And I should give him a reasonable date to reply by, not demand that he pay everything by then.

Hi [Name], I wanted to follow up about the welding machine payments. The last three €250 payments are still outstanding, so could you please let me know by [date] when you’ll be able to make the next €250 payment? It would also help if you could tell me what repayment schedule you can realistically manage for the rest of the amount you owe. I understand you may not be able to pay the full €750 at once—I just need us to agree on a clear plan and keep to it.
Yes, that says what I need without sounding aggressive. I’ll put in a date about a week from now and send it to him. Thanks.
You’re welcome. Giving him a week to respond while asking for a concrete payment date and realistic schedule strikes a good balance between being firm and keeping the tone respectful.
Right, I’ll send it as written and see what he comes back with.
That sounds sensible. I hope he responds with a clear and workable plan.
